operator_io_quirks: All table/column names are mixed-case CamelCase (Categories, OrderDetails, CustomerID); generated SQL must double-quote them and column lookup must be case-insensitive.
No spaces in identifiers here, but BIRD convention still requires quoting; DDL text has tabs before FOREIGN KEY lines (line-based unique/check scan must tolerate tabs).
All PKs are INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT; sqlite auto-assigns rowid when NULL inserted, so PK sampler values may be overridden silently on insert.
BirthDate declared DATE and OrderDate declared DATETIME but both stored as TEXT 'YYYY-MM-DD' (no time component); storage class contradicts declared type.
Date dispatch: first element '1968-12-08' does not parse as int, so Date fuzzer with template %Y-%m-%d; OrderDate same.
Price REAL DEFAULT 0, storage real, values like 18.0/21.35; Number fuzzer with scale from REAL (no args) -> default scale.
Quantity INTEGER distinct 43, values 5..40; Number fuzzer will produce negatives/perturbations implausible for quantity.
PostalCode TEXT with mixed formats ('12209','WA1 1DP','S-958 22','100'); String fuzzer will not preserve format.
Phone TEXT with formats '(503) 555-9831','(98) 598 76 54'; String fuzzer random charset a-zA-Z 0-9() will produce plausible-looking but wrong phones.
All FK parents exist and are unique PKs; no dangling FKs, no composite keys, no self-references, no non-unique parents.
All columns notnull=0 and null_rate=0.0; NOT NULL never enforced, so TS NULLs from empty parents never occur here.
Small tables (max 518 rows); no huge-table sampling concern, full read fine.
operator_ts_expectations: Number fuzzer on all *_ID columns: uniform in [-10^scale,10^scale] then +-1/+-2 perturbation; produces negative and huge IDs implausible for keys -> likely FN on ID-range predicates.

FK columns (Products.SupplierID/CategoryID, Orders.CustomerID/EmployeeID/ShipperID, OrderDetails.OrderID/ProductID) drawn from parent's final values with replacement -> duplicates and ties present, good for join/group queries.
String fuzzer on names/cities/countries: random charset strings plus contamination; destroys 'Germany'/'London' style values -> FN on equality predicates on Country/City.
Date fuzzer on BirthDate/OrderDate: template %Y-%m-%d, range from min/max of 5 sampled originals; produces dates outside 1996-1998 order window -> FN on date-range predicates.
Price REAL: Number fuzzer with default scale, list range quirk (upper end overwritten to full range) -> prices can be negative or huge -> FN on price thresholds.
Quantity INTEGER: Number fuzzer produces negatives and perturbations -> FN on quantity>0 style predicates.
PostalCode/Phone/Unit: String fuzzer random -> format predicates (LIKE 'WA%', phone patterns) fail -> FN.
PK uniqueness enforced by sample_fresh_primary_keys; single-column PK gets max_l0=inf so fresh draws always allowed -> many distinct IDs, few ties on PK.
Small parent tables (Shippers 3, Categories 8, Employees 10) sampled with replacement -> heavy duplication in child FK columns, good for COUNT/GROUP BY ties.
No NOT NULL/CHECK constraints -> no insert failures expected; rows_ok should equal requested sizes.
AUTOINCREMENT PK: if TS inserts NULL PK, sqlite assigns sequential rowids, so PK values may not match sampler output but remain unique.
No composite keys, no unique non-PK columns -> drop_unique_duplicates is a no-op here.
